Ben / Olivia — I dug into AR and the ledger. Summary below.

What I found:
- The credit CR-328 (issued 2027-05-18) was received and posted to unapplied credits on 2027-05-19. It was never applied to RF-5412 due to a remit-key mismatch (customer used old remit ref).
- Payment P-8721 from 2027-06-09 did apply correctly to RF-5412; the second remittance line in your CSV matches CR-328 but because of remit-key mismatch it remained unapplied.
- In our AR subledger RF-5412 shows VAT flagged as 0% because the billing entity on the invoice is the US entity. The customer should have been billed under Redwood EU (20% VAT).

Recommended actions (minimize revenue timing impact):
1) Apply CR-328 split: post JV to move credit from unapplied credits to RF-5412 (apply just the credit amount).
2) Post correcting JV to reclass VAT: debit Sales (EUR) and credit VAT payable (EU) for the VAT component (we'll calculate amounts below). This keeps revenue recognition untouched for the original cash receipts period but corrects the tax accrual.
3) No need to reissue invoice RF-5412 if FinOptics confirms acceptance of JV correction; if they want an invoice reissue for their audit, we can re-bill under EU entity and issue a credit + new invoice (longer path).

Proposed journal (summary):
- JE 20270611-AR-APPLY: Dr Unapplied Credits 15,240.00 EUR / Cr Accounts Receivable - RF-5412 15,240.00 EUR
- JE 20270611-VAT-RECLASS: Dr Sales (US->EU reclass) 2,540.00 EUR / Cr VAT Payable (EU) 2,540.00 EUR

I've attached JE_20270611.pdf with line-level calculations and the GL account strings. Grace — can you please OK the proposed JEs (or suggest modifications) so we can post on Monday?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
AR Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: JE_20270611.pdf (PDF, calculations + GL strings)
